tools.name: search_buyers
tools.description: Search DataWorth AI's directory of companies and programs that license a business's operating records (email, chat, files, CRM, code, CAD) to AI developers. Facts come from each company's own site; payouts are quoted in its own words and are not offers. Results are alphabetical (or by text relevance

tools.name: get_buyer
tools.description: Full directory entry for one buyer or program by its id (slug), e.g. 'lunchbreak', 'micro1-enterprise', 'turing-lazarus'. Includes its own quoted rules, sources and last-verified date.

tools.name: list_situations
tools.description: The directory's situation lists (closed or winding-down companies, under 30 employees, outside the US, source code, engineering/CAD, professional services) with the buyers in each and the page link.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Use when someone asks whether a specific company qualifies to license its records to AI data buyers. Compares the company's industry, size, years, country, status and number of business systems with the published eligibility rules of every buyer in DataWorth AI's directory that publishes clear rules

tools.name: get_changelog
tools.description: What changed in the buyer directory and when (newest first), plus what was left out and why.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_buyers, check_fit · Private data: search_buyers, check_fit · Public sink: search_buyers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_buyers, check_fit · Private data: search_buyers, check_fit · Public sink: search_buyers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
